title: Where Malware Protection and ATP checks fall in the web enforcement order

prose.text: Where a check falls decides which block the user sees. Three orders apply, depending on what the web module is looking at. {{first-violation-blocks}}

What an exception skips is in [[zia.atp.security-exceptions]]; the denylist check is [[zia.atp.blocked-urls]]; country blocking is [[zia.atp.blocked-countries]]; Page Risk is [[zia.atp.page-risk]]. Domain-level checks on encrypted traffic happen before decryption: [[zia.ssl-inspection.pipeline]]. Cloud App Control and URL Filtering ordering is in [[zia.cloud-app-control.precedence]] and [[zia.url-filtering.rule-order]].

checks.do: Whether the transaction is a GET request, a POST request or a response, since each has its own order.
Which numbered step is the earliest one that could have fired, since the first violation blocks the transaction.

first-violation-blocks.statement: When the web module finds a transaction violates a policy, the Public Service Edge blocks it immediately and does not enforce the policies that follow; the firewall module does not evaluate it, though firewall logs still show the web transaction as blocked.

quotes: In each case, when the web module determines that a transaction violates a specific policy, the Public Service Edge immediately blocks that transaction and does not continue enforcing the policies that follow.
The Public Service Edge also does not send the traffic to the Firewall module for policy evaluation.
However, your Firewall logs show that the user's web transaction is blocked.

get-order.statement: For an HTTP GET request the order is: 1 Custom Malicious URLs (ATP denylist), 2 Cloud App Control, 3 URL Filtering, 4 Security Exceptions, 5 Browser Control, 6 Country-Based Blocking, 7 IPS Signature Detection, 8 Suspicious Content Protection (Page Risk), 9 P2P Control, 10 Bandwidth Control. Malware Protection and Sandbox are not in the GET request list.

quotes: (i.e., The Public Service Edge checks if the URL exists on the organization's custom Advanced Threat Protection denylist).
8. Suspicious Content Protection (Advanced Threat Protection): The Public Service Edge calculates the Suspicious Content Protection (Page RiskTM) value
based on your organization's Bandwidth Control policy and the current bandwidth usage at the user's location. - HTTP POST Request
evidence.after: This is a user request to retrieve a resource from the web (e.g., a web page).

get-order.conditions: The absence of Malware Protection from the GET list is read from the document's list; files in GET responses are covered by the response order.

post-order.statement: For an HTTP POST request the order is: 1 Custom Malicious URLs, 2 Cloud App Control, 3 URL Filtering, 4 Security Exceptions, 5 Browser Control, 6 Country-Based Blocking, 7 Malicious URL Block (an extensive URL database), 8 IPS Signature Detection, 9 Suspicious Content Protection, 10 Malware Protection, 11 File Type Control, 12 Data Loss Prevention, 13 P2P Controls, 14 Bandwidth Control.

quotes: 7. Malicious URL Block (Advanced Threat Protection): The Public Service Edge checks if the requested URL is known to have malicious content using an extensive URL database that is updated daily with feeds from various partners.
evidence.after: This is a user request to submit or post data to the web

response-order.statement: For an HTTP response the order is: 1 Security Exceptions, 2 IPS Signature Detection, 3 Suspicious Content Protection, 4 Sandbox check for known malicious files, 5 Malware Protection, 6 File Type Control, 7 Sandbox analysis of unknown files, 8 AI/ML-based content categorization, 9 Bandwidth Control.

quotes: the current bandwidth usage at the user's location. - The following diagram summarizes the order of policy enforcement for different HTTP traffic types
evidence.after: This is data sent from the destination host back to the user in response to an HTTP GET

response-omits-url-checks.statement: The custom malicious URL list and country blocking, which the GET and POST request orders include, are not among the nine steps of the response order.
response-omits-url-checks.conditions: Read from the absence of those checks in the document's numbered response list, which ends at step 9 before the diagram; the document does not state the omission itself.

mp-after-atp-checks.statement: In the POST request and in the response, the Malware Protection check comes after the ATP checks, so an ATP block ends the transaction before file scanning would run.
mp-after-atp-checks.conditions: Derived from the listed order and the stop-at-first-violation rule.
